additional_info.subject: RE: ID0427713-DC/Si-D/FI-[MP/P9 170001028] Charging Issue CRM:02889000045
additional_info.body:
Hello,
There were atleast these this morning.
Costumer called and I asked more details.
The issue seems to be happening only in DC1. This is their dedicated outlet for charging their trucks.
In that outlet no issue with normal 400 V cars. But Trucks are sometimes not able to charge or they charge ounly couple of minutes then the charging ends.
I was able to see the sessions in SCB by filtering From time 2025-05-30T05:20:15.287Z to 2025-05-30T06:20:15.287Z
Then Ctrl + F “EVSE_NowVol[V]=7” so I can see the 700+ V charging sessions. All seemed to be very short.
Could this be a contactor fault since I see that we have issue with that. OR EcoG

additional_info.subject: ID0427713-DC/Si-D/FI-[MP/P9 170001028] Charging Issue CRM:02889000045
additional_info.body:
Hi Sakari, good morning.
Thanks for the reply. I can see the sessions failing with ERR67 or ERR35 which is PilotState dropped from C to B.
The best I can offer here is that, the charger cannot have a problem since, as you mentioned, 400V EVs don't have any problem.
We can install the EcoG 1.4.12 and see if it improves the situation (I don't really think so) but if it doesn't, we have access to the .pcap files in order to forward to the customer to give to the EV manufacturer for a follow up.
Can you ask the customer what is the EV brand and model?
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco
